purpose: Task B preparation: the wide decoder lanes' clock on an UltraScale+ part, as an estimate for AWS F2's VU47P, which the free Vivado licence does not cover
f2_clocks: clk_main_a0 fixed at 250 MHz; recipe clocks include 225 (B2), 200 (C1, C3), 187.5 (A0) and 150 MHz (C1); own MMCMs allowed (F2 Clock Recipes User Guide)
stand_in_part: xcku5p-ffvb676-2-e: Kintex UltraScale+, the same -2 speed grade; covered by the free Vivado Basic licence (2026.1 tier table)
tool: Vivado 2026.1 (Vivado Basic licence), out of context, model/perf/probes/usplus_timing.tcl: place ExtraTimingOpt, phys_opt AggressiveExplore, route AggressiveExplore, post-route phys_opt AggressiveExplore (as build_batch.tcl with VIVADO_EFFORT=high); each stage a separate process capped at 9 GB

designs.1: usplus_batch_top.sv: one lane (bench_lane.sv, FAST=2) in the batched harness (uart_batch_core.sv), as on the board; one synthesis
designs.15: usplus_lanes_top.sv: 15 lanes (bench_lane.sv, FAST=2) with registered inputs and folded outputs, without the UART core; one lane synthesized on its own (stage lane) and its netlist placed in all 15

result: 250 MHz met with 1 and with 15 lanes; worst path inside a decoder: the wide core's Huffman decoder (bit window -> code table -> block descriptor queue write), +0.573 ns with one lane, +0.336 ns with 15; with 15 lanes the overall worst path (+0.061 ns) is a lane's reset fan-out (in_rst, 637 loads), routing only

comparison_artix7.xc7a200tfbg484-2, 15 lanes: 141.5 MHz (-0.399 ns at 150 MHz, every lane on the Huffman bit-window loop)

side_finding: uart_batch_core.sv with 15 lanes needs more than 9 GB to synthesize on the KU5P even with the lanes as black boxes (killed twice at the cap; -resource_sharing off did not help), while one lane needs 3.5 GB: the 11.2 GB synthesis peak of the Artix-7 batch build came from the UART core's per-lane bookkeeping, not from the decoders
caveats: a stand-in: the VU47P has three SLRs (dies) and the AWS shell takes part of it; SLR crossings, the shell and its memory interfaces are not modelled
15 lanes fill 45 % of the KU5P's LUTs (68 % on the Artix-7 batch); a fuller chip may lose more margin
out of context: the clock enters on a port that drives a BUFG and one BUFGCE per lane; on F2 it comes from the shell
a timing estimate only: no board, no bitstream
